structural_change: sp7d (SQC-QDIE5 10-22, parallel FB to sp7c): sp6b outline height 518.4 (W pin face unchanged) and sp6b row lattice (8 rows pitch 43.2, CTS passed there at 60.7/41.3 ps spread) + sp7c ck_ingest entry pin in the W face interior; only the 3 inter-column channels that receive each SRAM's ~270-pin 20.8-um W edge are widened 24.2 -> 56.6 um (column pitch 75.6 -> 108.0), outline 475.2 -> 572.4 wide (< 600 um clock span); sp6b GRT overflow 3,915 sat in exactly those 24-um channels (hot x 150-300 / y 175-350). sp7c (SQC-QDIE5 10-22): sp7b macro lattice/outline unchanged; the ck_ingest clock entry pin moves from the SW end of the W face to the face interior (after eng_indata, ~62% of the 1,245 W pins) beside the pin-flop mass: sp7a CTS FAILED ck_ingest boundary pin-flop spread 138.4 ps > 80 TT with the entry at (0,0) and pin flops over the full 518-um face. sp6a/sp6b gate GRT congestion (sp6a 388.8x561.6 total overflow 139,692; sp6b 475.2x518.4 3,915 at 23% usage) is local: hot gcells x 150-300 / y 175-350 = the 75.6x43.2 macro lattice channels; each 32x128 SRAM has ~270 M4 pins on its 20.8-um W edge (macro OBS M1-M4), so std cells + M4 escapes crowd 24-um channels. sp7b: same source/pins/clocks, macros re-pitched: 4 columns pitch 118.8 um (67.4 um channel), 8 rows pitch 64.8 um (44 um row gap); outline 626.4x583.2 (enlarge, owner 10-21). sp6 CTS spread/timing (+91/+107 ps) were fine.
